text:
anne: FYI starting a short spike to extract the enrichment capability into a pluggable adapter + compatibility shim. want quick feedback on safety nets and cutover strategy.

michael: +1. smaller interface surface so we can iterate. prefer a minimal 'Enricher' API that the gateway can call directly.

michael: sketch:
```
interface Enricher {
  enrich(ctx, input): Enriched
}
```
keep a default shim that proxies to the monolith until we're confident.

priya: agree. also require telemetry hooks and a per-tenant canary flag. metrics to track: success_rate, avg_latency_ms, token_delta, and regression_score_on_eval_set.

dave: big question: who owns the KV cache during the transition? we need a plan for cache consistency or a read-through mirror. double-writes are risky.

anne: good point. plan proposal: phase 1 = read-through shim (new adapter reads from new plugin but falls back to monolith; writes still go to monolith). no writes until reconciliation in phase 3.

priya: rollout plan: cohorted tenants -> run canary traffic + run full eval prompt set per-cohort. hook alerts to regression_score + error_rate. automatic rollback if regression > threshold.

michael: add code guardrails: feature-flag gating, runtime kill-switch, circuit-breaker on the gateway side. keep adapter idempotent.

deploy-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/enricher-shim/pull/482 — includes unit tests, integration harness, and a canary runner that can replay recorded traffic.

anne: ok I'll draft a short RFC and migration checklist (tests needed, metrics, rollback playbook, ownership matrix). ping me if you want to join the spike. :coffee:
